parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is declared as domain layer. That is most likely because its path matches the domain pattern **/core/**, even though it also matches the application patterns **/application/**, **/usecases/** and **/*.usecase.ts. Judged against the declared domain role, the file carries application-kind responsibilities. CreatePaymentIntentUseCase.execute() runs a whole workflow: it resolves an external payment gateway, calls it to create a payment intent, builds the Payment entity, sets the intent details, saves the entity through the repository, and maps failures to UseCaseError. Coordinating external gateways and persistence like this is application work, not domain logic. The class also carries the NestJS @Injectable() decorator, which is framework wiring and does not belong in a domain file. The responsibilities fit the application layer well, so the main problem is probably the layer assignment. As the unit is declared, though, it does not match the domain role.
